ei.title: The Ripple Effect of One Kind Gesture
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: The sun shone in the cloudless sky as Becky, a retired teacher, walked to the fruit market. Across town, Dana was riding a bus towards the museum for a job interview. Just before reaching her stop, Dana noticed the sky had suddenly darkened. Her heart sank — she had no umbrella. As she stepped off the bus next to the market, where Becky had just finished shopping, raindrops began to fall. Dana felt panic. She didn't want to show up to her interview soaked. She looked around but couldn't find any stores nearby to buy an umbrella, and she didn't have time to search around. Just then, Becky approached her, holding an open umbrella in one hand and a closed one in the other. "Take this," she said with a smile. Dana's eyes widened. "Are you sure?" Becky nodded. "I always carry an extra on rainy days." Dana thanked her, took the umbrella, and opened it. She saw a small card tied to the handle. It read: "Cover each other." She was touched by the message. She hurried to the museum, arriving dry and comfortable, and performed well in her interview. The Museum CEO was impressed by Dana and offered her the Event Manager position, her dream job. Throughout the years ahead, she often thought back to Becky's kind gesture. Inspired by the memory, Dana created a museum event called "Cover Each Other" with paintings of people supporting others. She donated half of the money from ticket sales to families who lost their homes to natural disasters. Dana kept Becky's message framed in her office as a reminder that one kind gesture could change someone's life. The kindness of one stranger had shaped her path, and she made sure it continued to shape the world.

det.korean: (A) darkened=어두워진, (B) panic=당황/공황, (C) widened=커졌다/넓어졌다

✅ ① darkened — panic — widened: 원문 일치. 하늘이 갑자기 어두워지고(darkened), Dana가 당황하며(panic), 우산을 받고 눈이 커졌다(widened)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답

❌ ③ darkened — relief — widened: (B) relief(안도)는 우산이 없어 당황한 panic과 반대 감정
❌ ④ darkened — panic — narrowed: (C) narrowed(가늘어진)는 놀라 눈이 커진 widened와 반대
det.tip: the sky had suddenly darkened(어두워진) / Dana felt panic(당황) / Dana's eyes widened(커졌다)

As she stepped off the bus next to the market, where Becky had just finished shopping, raindrops began to fall. Dana felt panic. She didn't want to show up to her interview soaked. She looked around but couldn't find any stores nearby to buy an umbrella, and she didn't have time to search around. Just then, Becky approached her, holding an open umbrella in one hand and a closed one in the other. "Take this," she said with a smile. Dana's eyes widened. "Are you sure?" Becky nodded. "I always carry an extra on rainy days." Dana thanked her, took the umbrella, and opened it. She saw a small card tied to the handle. It read: "Cover each other." She was touched by the message. She <u>hurried</u> to the museum, arriving dry and comfortable, and performed well in her interview. The Museum CEO was impressed by Dana and offered her the Event Manager position, her dream job. Throughout the years ahead, she often thought back to Becky's kind gesture. Inspired by the memory, Dana created a museum event called "Cover Each Other" with paintings of people supporting others. She donated half of the money from ticket sales to families who lost their homes to natural disasters. Dana kept Becky's message framed in her office as a reminder that one kind gesture could change someone's life. The kindness of one stranger had shaped her path, and she made sure it continued to shape the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 hurried와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: hurried=서둘러 갔다 → rushed=서둘렀다
det.analysis:
✅ ① rushed: rushed(서둘렀다)는 hurried(서둘러 갔다)의 동의어 ←정답
❌ ② delayed: delayed(지연시켰다)는 서두름과 반대 의미
❌ ③ walked: walked(걸었다)는 속도감 없는 일반 이동으로 서두름의 뜻이 빠짐
❌ ④ paused: paused(멈췄다)는 서둘러 이동한 것과 반대
det.tip: hurried = rushed = hastened = 서두르다

det.korean: offered=제안했다/주었다 → presented=제시했다/주었다
det.analysis:
❌ ① refused: refused(거절했다)는 제안과 반대 의미
❌ ② demanded: demanded(요구했다)는 주는 것이 아니라 요구하는 것
❌ ③ ignored: ignored(무시했다)는 일자리를 제안한 맥락과 반대
✅ ④ presented: presented(제시했다/주었다)는 offered(제안했다)의 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: offered her the Event Manager position = presented = 제안했다, 주었다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 performed와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: performed well=잘 해냈다 → did well=잘 했다
det.analysis:
❌ ① struggled: struggled(고전했다)는 잘 해낸 것과 반대
✅ ② did: did(했다/해냈다)는 performed(해냈다)의 동의어로 'did well in her interview'처럼 쓰임 ←정답
❌ ③ prepared: prepared(준비했다)는 면접을 수행한 것이 아니라 사전 준비
❌ ④ rested: rested(쉬었다)는 면접을 수행한 맥락과 무관
det.tip: performed well = did well = 잘 해냈다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dry와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: dry=마른/젖지 않은 → wet=젖은
det.analysis:
❌ ① clean: clean(깨끗한)은 dry와 반대 개념이 아님
❌ ② warm: warm(따뜻한)은 온도 개념으로 dry의 반의어가 아님
✅ ③ wet: wet(젖은)은 dry(마른/젖지 않은)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ④ safe: safe(안전한)는 dry와 무관한 개념
det.tip: dry(마른/젖지 않은) ↔ wet(젖은)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 lost와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: lost=잃었다 → found=찾았다/얻었다
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandoned: abandoned(버렸다)는 잃은 것과 유사한 상실의 의미
❌ ② misplaced: misplaced(엉뚱한 곳에 두어 잃었다)는 lost와 비슷한 의미
❌ ③ dropped: dropped(떨어뜨렸다)는 잃음과 가까운 의미
✅ ④ found: found(찾았다/얻었다)는 lost(잃었다)의 반의어 ←정답
det.tip: lost(잃었다) ↔ found(찾았다)

questions.passage:
(A) He shifted his <u>position</u> on the sofa and stretched his legs to feel more comfortable.
(B) The Museum CEO was impressed by Dana and offered her the Event Manager <u>position</u>, her dream job.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 position의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: position: (A) 소파 위의 몸의 자세/위치 / (B) 제안받은 직책/일자리
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 자세/위치 — (B) 직책/일자리: (A)는 소파에서 몸의 자세를 바꾼 것, (B)는 Event Manager라는 직책을 제안받은 것으로 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 입장/견해 — (B) 직책/일자리: (A)의 position은 의견이 아닌 몸의 자세
❌ ③ (A) 자세/위치 — (B) 위치: (B)의 position은 장소가 아닌 직책
❌ ④ (A) 순위 — (B) 입장/견해: (A)는 순위가 아니고 (B)는 견해가 아님
det.tip: position: ① (명사) 자세/위치 ② (명사) 직책/일자리 ③ (명사) 입장/견해 ④ (동사) 배치하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a sudden feeling of strong fear that prevents you from thinking clearly"

det.korean: panic=공황/당황 (갑작스러운 강한 두려움으로 명료한 사고를 막는 것)
det.analysis:
❌ ① comfort: comfort(편안함)는 두려움과 반대되는 느낌
❌ ② wonder: wonder(경이로움)는 두려움이 아닌 감탄의 감정
✅ ③ panic: panic(공황/당황)은 갑작스러운 강한 두려움으로 사고를 막는다는 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ relief: relief(안도)는 두려움이 해소된 뒤의 감정
det.tip: panic = 공황/당황. a sudden feeling of strong fear가 핵심

questions.passage: Inspired by the memory, Dana created a museum event called "Cover Each Other" with paintings of people __________ (support) others. She donated half of the money from ticket sales to families who lost their homes to natural disasters.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 명사 people을 뒤에서 수식하는 현재분사(-ing)로 바꾼다
det.analysis: 'paintings of people ___ others'에서 앞의 명사 people을 능동적으로 수식하는 현재분사가 필요하다. people이 others를 '지지하는' 능동 관계이므로 support → supporting(현재분사)
det.tip: 명사 + V-ing(현재분사): people supporting others (~하는 사람들)

questions.passage: Dana kept Becky's message framed in her office as a reminder that one kind gesture could change someone's life. The kindness of one stranger had __________ (shape) her path, and she made sure it continued to shape the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 조동사 had 뒤에 과거분사를 써서 과거완료를 만든다 (had + p.p.)
det.analysis: 'The kindness ... had ___ her path'에서 had 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 과거완료가 된다. shape은 규칙 동사이므로 shape → shaped
det.tip: had + p.p.(과거완료): had shaped (~해 왔었다)

det.korean: thought back to=~을 회상했다 — 세월이 흘러도 Becky의 친절을 자주 떠올렸다는 맥락

det.korean: show up=나타나다/모습을 보이다 — 면접에 젖은 채로 나타나고 싶지 않았다는 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① give up: give up(포기하다)은 면접에 나타나는 맥락과 무관
✅ ② show up: 원문 일치. 흠뻑 젖은 채로 면접에 나타나고(show up) 싶지 않았다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ look back: look back(되돌아보다)은 모습을 드러내는 의미가 아님
❌ ④ drop by: drop by(잠깐 들르다)는 면접장에 격식 있게 나타나는 맥락과 어긋남
det.tip: She didn't want to show up to her interview soaked — 젖은 채로 나타나고 싶지 않았다
